successCriteria.description: The LeavePolicy domain model interface is exported from the leave-policy module and exposes exactly the reconciled LeavePolicy attributes (id, policyName, leaveTypeId, entitlementDays, accrualRate, maxAccumulation, minimumNoticeDays, requiresManagerApproval, isActive, createdAt, updatedAt), with the optional numeric fields typed as `number | undefined` and the boolean fields as `boolean`.

The ILeavePolicyRepository interface is exported and declares all seven required operations: findAll, findById, findByLeaveTypeId, findActiveByLeaveTypeId, create, update, delete — with the CreateLeavePolicyDto and UpdateLeavePolicyDto types co-located in the same file (Create DTO marks optional fields with `?`, Update DTO makes all fields optional).

The LeavePolicyRepository implementation persists and retrieves LeavePolicy rows against the `leave_policies` table using parameterized SQL ($1, $2, …) with explicit column lists (no SELECT *), and maps snake_case database rows to the camelCase LeavePolicy model, converting nullable optionals to `undefined`.

findActiveByLeaveTypeId returns only rows where is_active = true for the given leaveTypeId, distinguishing it from findByLeaveTypeId which returns all rows regardless of active status; both return arrays (or the appropriate empty array when no rows match).

create uses INSERT … RETURNING to persist a new LeavePolicy and returns the created entity, applying sensible defaults for omitted optional fields (e.g. isActive defaults to true, nullable numerics default to null); update dynamically builds a SET clause from only the provided fields, appends updated_at = NOW(), falls back to a findById lookup when no fields are provided, and returns null when the target row does not exist; delete returns a boolean indicating whether a row was removed.

The leave-policy barrel (index.ts) is extended — not replaced — to re-export the LeavePolicy model, ILeavePolicyRepository, LeavePolicyRepository, and both DTOs alongside the existing Phase 2 LeaveType exports, so downstream modules can import all leave-policy symbols from the single public entry point.

Jest unit tests in tests/unit/modules/leave-policy/ cover the LeavePolicyRepository by mocking the pg pool, asserting exact SQL strings and parameter arrays, and exercising found/not-found, empty-result, create-with-defaults, partial-update, no-fields-update, not-found-update, delete true/false, and custom-client-constructor paths — mirroring the Phase 2 leave-type repository test conventions.

constraints: GP-001 Repository pattern: all database access for leave_policies must go through the LeavePolicyRepository; no inline SQL or direct pool calls outside the repository implementation.
no-any: the repository and model must use `unknown` with type guards (or precise row interfaces) instead of `any`; strict TypeScript (strict: true, strict null checks) must pass with no implicit any.
no-direct-db-outside-repository: only the LeavePolicyRepository implementation may issue SQL against the leave_policies table; the model, interface, DTOs, and barrel must contain no database calls.
All SQL must use parameterized placeholders ($1, $2, …) with values passed separately — no string-interpolated user input — to prevent SQL injection.

Module dependency rule: the leave-policy module's internal files may import each other, but any cross-module access must go through the module's public index.ts barrel; the repository must obtain the pg Pool from src/shared/db/connection.ts (the shared connection module), not instantiate its own Pool.

The repository must accept an optional injectable queryable client (defaulting to the shared pool) so it can participate in caller-owned transactions per the Transaction Contract, mirroring the Phase 2 LeaveTypeRepository constructor pattern.
outOfScope: LeavePolicyService, its interface, entitlement/pro-ration calculation logic, and any business-rule enforcement (Phase 8).
Fastify routes, controllers, RBAC guards, and HTTP error-response mapping for leave policies (later phases).
Database migrations or schema DDL for the leave_policies table — the table schema is defined by reconciled architecture; this phase only reads/writes it.
LeaveBalance model/repository (Phase 4), LeaveRequest (Phase 5), AuditRecord (Phase 6), and Notification (Phase 7) modules.
Audit-record creation (GP-002) for LeavePolicy create/update/delete — the repository layer does not write audit records; audit integration belongs to the service layer in a later phase.

entityInvariants.invariant: A LeavePolicy is always associated with exactly one LeaveType via leaveTypeId, which must reference an existing row in leave_types (FK constraint); a policy cannot exist without a parent leave type.

A LeavePolicy has an ACTIVE/INACTIVE lifecycle governed by the isActive flag; only policies with isActive = true may be used for request validation and balance initialization (binding business rule 8). The repository's findActiveByLeaveTypeId must surface only active policies.

entitlementDays is a non-negative quantity representing the annual lump-sum allocation; accrualRate, maxAccumulation, and minimumNoticeDays are optional policy modifiers that, when present, constrain accrual caps and advance-notice requirements respectively. The repository must preserve optionality (undefined when the DB column is null).

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns all LeavePolicy rows (mapped to the model); returns an empty array when none exist. Rejects on database error.
Returns the matching LeavePolicy or null when no row has the given id. Rejects on database error.
Returns all LeavePolicy rows for the given leaveTypeId (any active state); returns an empty array when none match. Rejects on database error.
Returns only LeavePolicy rows where is_active = true for the given leaveTypeId; returns an empty array when none match. Rejects on database error.

Inserts a new leave_policies row and returns the created LeavePolicy (via INSERT … RETURNING). Applies defaults for omitted optional fields. Rejects on constraint violation (e.g. invalid leave_type_id FK).

Updates only the provided fields (dynamic SET), sets updated_at = NOW(), and returns the updated LeavePolicy or null if no row matches the id; when no fields are provided, returns the current row (or null if absent) without mutation. Rejects on database error.
Deletes the row with the given id and returns true if a row was removed, false if no row matched. Rejects on database error.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The LeavePolicyRepository implementation must mirror the structural conventions established by the Phase 2 LeaveTypeRepository: Queryable type (Pick<Pool, 'query'>), constructor(client?: Queryable) defaulting to the shared pool, a private snake_case *Row interface, a rowTo* mapper converting snake_case→camelCase with `?? undefined` for nullable optionals, parameterized SQL with explicit column lists (no SELECT *), INSERT … RETURNING for create, dynamic SET-clause builder with a paramIndex counter plus updated_at = NOW() and findById fallback for update, and boolean rowCount-based return for delete.

The ILeavePolicyRepository interface and its co-located CreateLeavePolicyDto/UpdateLeavePolicyDto must follow the same DTO convention as the Phase 2 leave-type interface file: Create DTO marks optional fields with `?` and required fields plain; Update DTO makes every field optional with `?`; the repository interface declares async methods returning the model, model | null, model[], or boolean as appropriate.

The leave-policy barrel must be extended (not replaced) so that the existing Phase 2 re-exports (LeaveType, ILeaveTypeRepository, CreateLeaveTypeDto, UpdateLeaveTypeDto, LeaveTypeRepository) remain intact and the new Phase 3 symbols (LeavePolicy, ILeavePolicyRepository, CreateLeavePolicyDto, UpdateLeavePolicyDto, LeavePolicyRepository) are added alongside them.

The LeavePolicyRepository unit tests must follow the Phase 2 leave-type repository test conventions: jest.mock the shared db connection before importing pool, a makeRow(overrides) helper returning a full snake_case row with defaults, beforeEach resetting the mock and constructing the repository, assertions on exact SQL strings and exact parameter arrays via toHaveBeenCalledWith, and a custom-client constructor test verifying the injected client is used instead of the default pool.

The LeavePolicy model attributes and the leave_policies table column set must match the reconciled architecture exactly: model fields id, policyName, leaveTypeId, entitlementDays, accrualRate, maxAccumulation, minimumNoticeDays, requiresManagerApproval, isActive, createdAt, updatedAt; table columns id, policy_name, leave_type_id (FK→leave_types.id), entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at.

integrationPoints.why: The LeavePolicyRepository obtains the shared PostgreSQL pool from this module (defaulting to it when no client is injected), consistent with GP-001 and the Phase 2 repository pattern.
LeavePolicy.leaveTypeId is a foreign key to leave_types.id; the repository reads/writes this relationship. Phase 3 depends on the Phase 2 leave-type model and barrel being present and importable.

integrationPoints.target: leave-balance module (Phase 4) and leave-policy service (Phase 8) — downstream consumers
integrationPoints.why: LeaveBalance.policyId will reference leave_policies.id, and LeavePolicyService will consume ILeavePolicyRepository to look up active policies and compute entitlements; this phase establishes the repository contract those later phases depend on.
